content.text:
No, the two new commits don't touch what goes wrong in any of the three cases. I reread all 40 runs of each case, 20 with the branch and 20 without, from the logs I already had, so this cost nothing. Two cases didn't get worse. One really changed.

**Not worse:**
- **`connect-verified-close`: 0 of 20 passed without the branch, 2 of 20 with it.** Both fail the same way: after the app says the connection is verified, the model replies with no text at all.
- **`add-many-fit`: 11 of 20 without the branch, 9 of 20 with it.** Every failure on both sides is the same one, offering 5 to 8 choices where fewer are wanted. A difference of 2 in 20 runs is what chance alone produces.

**Really changed: `add-then-undo`.** A person names an A1 mini and the model adds it. The prompt says the model must then end its reply with "Want to connect it so you can send prints straight to it?" and the choices "Connect it | Not now". In 5 of the 20 runs with the branch, the model instead said "Let me check if it can be found on your network" and called the network check unasked. That never happened in the 20 runs without the branch.

The test runner crashed exactly at that call, which is why those 5 runs showed up as errors rather than failures. The crash hid the behavior change. The runner fix now lets those runs finish, but the model's behavior is the same.

**Why, as a hypothesis I haven't tested:** the connection-skills commit reworded the prompt's connecting rule. It used to say "for a Bambu Lab printer, call printer_connection_status and connect to a printer it lists". It now says "start with printer_connection_status; the app then adds how that connection works". The model may read "start with" as "do this first", even right after adding. The other suspect is the network check's own description, which the same commit made several times longer.

**A separate, older problem:** a silent reply after an app note. It's most of the failures in the verified-close case (19 of 20 without the branch) and 8 of 20 add-then-undo runs on both sides. It already happens on `jusprin-newui`, so merging the branch doesn't make it worse. I'd give it its own investigation rather than hold this branch for it.

I agree with your order: fix the real change first, then run the full regression on the final tip.

**Decision needed: may I spend live runs to find the cause of the unasked network check?** It's your call because it's paid model use. The plan is to run `add-then-undo` and `add-named-model` 20 times each on DeepSeek V4 Flash, three ways:
- on the current tip;
- with the old connecting sentence put back;
- with the old network-check description put back.

That's 120 short chats. My estimate is about $4: around four requests a chat at roughly $0.0075 each, as measured by the connection-skill session, plus OpenRouter's fee for any searches the model makes. Then I'd change the wording that's at fault and rerun both cases to confirm. The branch is checked out by [the connection-skill session](#local_4a3a2148-75ed-49b8-ad21-50ea4b91b065), so I'll do the experiments in my own worktree and tell it before I commit. My pick is to run it now. The other option is to merge with the unasked check still in, which skips the connect offer for about one person in four.
